blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A server works in the Inspector, but the host cannot start it from its configuration file, which gives a relative path to the data folder. What does the documentation blame?

options.text: A host can launch only servers that were first registered with the Inspector
options.says: Ruled out because the guide says "the same principles apply to any stdio-based MCP client", and no registration with the Inspector exists.

options.text: The directory can be undefined, so locations should be written in full
options.says: The third page quotes the guide: the directory of a launched server "may be undefined (like / on macOS) since the client could be started from anywhere", so use absolute paths.

options.text: A host can pass along no environment variables, so the data path is lost
options.says: Ruled out because servers "inherit only a limited subset of environment variables automatically", which is some of them and not none.

options.text: Relative paths can resolve only when the server runs over Streamable HTTP
options.says: Ruled out because "testing from the command line uses the directory where you run the command", which is the contrast, and the transport is not part of it.

origin.section: Where a server fails in front of a host

questions.stem: Under the 2026-07-28 revision, a server needs to ask the user a question in the middle of a call, but the incoming call declared no matching feature. What does the server return?

options.text: An unsupported-version error that lists the versions it accepts
options.says: Ruled out because an unsupported-version error is one that "lists the server's supported versions in its data field", and the version was fine here.

options.text: An invalid-params error, since the metadata fields are absent
options.says: Ruled out because "A request missing either required field is rejected with error -32602", and the required fields were sent.

options.text: A missing-capability error, naming whatever the metadata omitted
options.says: The third page says that if the server needs a capability that the request's client capabilities did not declare, "it returns a MissingRequiredClientCapabilityError (code -32021) naming the missing capabilities".

options.text: A tool result flagged as an error, saying the user cannot be reached
options.says: Ruled out because the error is "returned as an error with its own code", so a client can tell it from a failed tool.

origin.section: Where a server fails in front of a host

questions.stem: A team must build an MCP server that speaks the newest protocol version. Which of the four SDKs used in the course reached that version when it was checked?

options.says: Ruled out because "only the Python one reached 2026-07-28 when it was checked".
Ruled out because the Kotlin SDK is one of those that "contain no support for 2026-07-28".
Ruled out because the TypeScript and Java SDKs have "their latest revision is 2025-11-25" as well.
The first page says the Python SDK speaks both eras, and that the other three "contain no support for 2026-07-28, and their latest revision is 2025-11-25".

questions.stem: A query matches no stored entries. How does the course's notes server answer?

options.text: With a tool error that tells the model to ask the user for a new query
options.says: Ruled out because the answer is "which is not an error", so there is no tool error to read.

options.text: With ordinary text saying that nothing fits, and the error flag stays off
options.says: The third page says that with no match the search answers `No notes match "{query}"`, in the practice statement's words "which is not an error".

options.text: With a resource error for the missing note, as for a bad id
options.says: Ruled out because the protocol error that says `No note {id}` is "for reading a note that does not exist", and "a search that finds nothing is a normal answer".

options.text: With a protocol error, as for an unknown tool, so that the client logs it
options.says: Ruled out because protocol errors "indicate issues with the request structure itself that models are less likely to be able to fix", and the request here is valid.
